title: Side by side

brief.story: The bench needs two indicator LEDs, but this corner's 9 V supply is budgeted at 20 mA. Both LEDs still have to be clearly lit.
brief.goal: Light LED1 and LED2 at 12 mA or more each, while the supply delivers no more than 20 mA.

hints: In parallel, each LED takes its own current and the supply pays for both. In series, the same current flows through one LED and then the other.
Chain them: supply column 3 → resistor → LED1's anode (column 10). Then a jumper from LED1's cathode (column 12) to LED2's anode (column 16). LED2's cathode is already wired to ground.
In series the two LEDs take 2.0 V each, so the resistor gets 9 − 2 − 2 = 5 V. For 15 mA: R = 5 V / 0.015 A ≈ 330 Ω.

spec.explain: Side by side, each LED needs its own current and the supply has to deliver the sum. In series, one current passes through both.

debrief: In series, one current does both jobs: the 15 mA through LED1 is the same 15 mA through LED2, so the supply only delivers 15 mA. The voltages add up instead: 2 V + 2 V across the LEDs and 5 V across the resistor make the supply's 9 V. In parallel it's the other way round: every branch gets the same voltage, and the currents add. That's the whole difference between series and parallel.
